column1: # CodeBrix.LilyPort -- THE D43 PORT-GENERATED BASELINE (ruling R9, Jeremy, 2026-08-16).
# WHAT THIS IS.  Six regression pages whose ONLY divergence from the oracle is the
# glyph-outline skyline debug drawing, frozen from the port's own output and graded
# against the port's own output thereafter:
#     python3 compare-output.py --baseline baseline/svg candidate/svg
# Expect 6 of 6 MATCH.  --baseline is load-bearing and is not a convenience: without
# it the baseline side resolves its glyph paths against the ORACLE's half of
# glyph-identity.tsv, 5 of 73 resolve, and all six rows read GLYPHS-DIFFER.  That is
# the control, and it was run.
# WHAT IT CLAIMS -- NO DRIFT, AND NOTHING ELSE.  Rule 33 forbids an expected value
# recorded from the port's own output, and this is exactly that, so it must never be
# read as a correctness result.  The CORRECTNESS claim for this mechanism is carried
# by GlyphOutlineSkylineTests in the Engine suite, whose expected segment counts are
# computed from upstream's own max (2, chord / 0.2) with a scale control that a table
# returning a constant cannot fake.  LANDING THE BASELINE WITHOUT THAT FENCE IS THE
# FAILURE MODE; the two are not interchangeable.
# WHY THESE SIX CANNOT BE GRADED AGAINST THE ORACLE.  The port BUILDS Emmentaler from
# the Metafont sources on purpose (D13/D23's neighbour, tools/font-build/).  That
# build is not outline-identical to the oracle's: MEASURED from the committed
# glyph-identity index on 2026-08-16, 277 of emmentaler-20's 662 glyph outlines
# serialize identically between the two builds and 385 do not.  Every glyph DIMENSION
# is read from the LILC table, which IS byte-identical -- which is why 2,208 rows
# match and only the one mechanism that reads the OUTLINE does not.  Re-measured the
# same day: accidentals.sharp, whose outline is IDENTICAL between the builds, is the
# control and its skyline already agrees with the oracle exactly; clefs.G and
# noteheads.s2 differ.  The divergence is confined to glyphs whose outlines differ.
# Full account: Engine PORT-COVERAGE, "GLYPH-OUTLINE SKYLINES DIFFER BECAUSE THE TWO
# EMMENTALER BUILDS DIFFER".
# /!\ RE-FREEZING.  Only from a FRESH full sweep, never from whatever candidate/svg
# happens to be on disk, and only with a recorded reason -- a baseline re-frozen to
# make a red row green has destroyed the only thing it was for.  These six rows STILL
# grade GLYPHS-DIFFER against the oracle corpus in the ordinary sweep, and still floor
# there; being graded here is a statement about G1, not about the measurement.
# /!\ NOT THE G1 SKIP LIST.  Nothing here is skipped.  g1-skip-list.tsv holds the eight
# rows ruled OUT of G1 (R8(A)/D31); these six are ruled IN and graded, against this.
# frozen: 2026-08-16, PARITY 15, from the sweep of 2026-08-16 07:44-07:52
#         (2,146 files: 2,121 svg, 25 no output, 0 errored; self-check 2,317 == 2,317)
# RE-FROZEN 2026-08-16, PARITY 16 -- ONE FILE, skyline-grob-rotation.svg, and the
# reason is recorded because a baseline that is re-frozen silently claims nothing.
# PARITY 16 restored upstream's three-way item split in Paper_column_engraver, so a
# tied unforced accidental -- a break reminder -- stopped reserving width it never
# draws (see PORT-COVERAGE, CONDITIONAL ITEMS).  That is a deliberate, separately
# fenced spacing fix worth 10 corpus rows, and moving the music necessarily reshapes
# the DEBUG SKYLINE drawn over it: the page gained 20 line segments.  A/B'd -- with
# the fix reverted the row returns to the old bytes exactly, and the other five
# baseline pages are byte-identical either way, which is what makes this one file's
# change attributable rather than drift.
# EXTENDED 2026-08-17, PARITY 20 -- TWO ROWS, ruling R15 (Jeremy, 2026-08-17), option (a).
# `accidental-ancient.svg' and `markup-with-true-dimensions.svg' are D43's class exactly:
# their ONLY divergence from the oracle is our own Emmentaler build's outlines, and it is
# measured to the FONT UNIT rather than merely bounded.  One font unit is 0.004 staff
# spaces (upem 1000; emmentaler-20's em is the 20pt staff height = 4 staff spaces):
#   accidental-ancient          -0.0120 = 3 units, accidentals.hufnagelM1 (port 147, oracle 144)
#   markup-with-true-dimensions +0.0127 = 1 unit x 2^(10/6), scripts.trill (port -323, oracle -322)
#                               +0.0254 = the same, twice; the file is \fontsize #10 (x3.1748)
# The attribution is COMPLETE, not merely consistent: drift.py reports accidental-ancient
# moving exactly ONE mark and markup-with-true-dimensions exactly TWELVE, and the
# comparator names those same two glyphs.  Nothing else on either page moves.  Measured
# with ft_decompose.py over both emmentaler-20 files, selfcheck run first.
# WHY ONLY THESE TWO ROWS OUT OF 2,316 -- and it is the same reason as the six above.
# Every glyph DIMENSION comes from the LILC table, which is byte-identical between the
# builds; the OUTLINE is consulted in one place (get_glyph_outline_bbox, feeding skylines)
# plus `\with-true-dimensions', which reads it by definition.  These two rows are the two
# pages that reach that path with a glyph whose outline differs.
# /!\ RECORDED IN 2026-08-02 AND IT NAMED ITS OWN SYMPTOM: tools/font-build/README.txt
# section 7 measured the bbox differences, named accidentals.mensuralM1 as one of the two
# largest, and named the one code path that would expose them.  Trap 27a.
# These two rows still read PLACEMENT-DIFFERS against the ORACLE corpus and floor there.
# That is EXPECTED and is not work.
# frozen: 2026-08-17, PARITY 20, from the sweep of 2026-08-17 02:08-02:15
#         (2,146 files: 2,121 svg, 25 no output, 0 errored; self-check 2,317 == 2,317).
#         PROVEN CURRENT rather than assumed: both pages were re-rendered from the
#         then-current binary into a scratch directory and compared byte for byte with
#         the sweep's output -- identical.
# /!\ THE CORRECTNESS CLAIM FOR THESE TWO IS NOT HERE EITHER.  Rule 33: this file records
# the port's own output.  GlyphOutlineSkylineTests gained
# `a_glyphs_true_extent_is_read_from_its_outline_and_not_from_its_declared_box', which
# asserts on BOTH of these rows' own glyphs that the true extent is the INK and that the
# ordinary extent of the same stencil is the LILC-declared box -- two readings, two
# tables -- with accidentals.sharp as the control, the glyph whose two sources agree.
# A/B'd by making a named glyph contribute its declared box instead of tracing its
# outline: the claim fails and the control still passes.
